proposed_from.topic: Exact attrition-robust randomization inference for an explicitly weighted fixed-count assignment support: under a sharp additive null, arbitrary treatment-indexed observation indicators, and Wilcoxon treated-rank sums with midranks, characterize the supremum exact upper-tail p-value over all legal missing-outcome completions by a complete weak-order chamber complex. Prove unconditional finite-sample validity, an explicit O((2n+1)^k n|Omega| poly(bits)) algorithm with a linear one-missing sweep, O(n^2) additive-effect inversion, and NP-completeness of EXPLICIT-MAX-TAIL for variable k by an explicit rational weighted-support CLIQUE reduction. Include the constrained six-unit non-extreme-completion witness, the equality-face witness, and a conditional saved-support corollary for a prospective cvcrand rank option on prespecified cluster endpoints; do not claim hardness for uniform balance-generated supports or unchanged cptest applicability. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Two independent presolves derived weak-order attainment and oracle-tail domination for arbitrary treatment-indexed masks; reconstructed the fixed-k and k=1 algorithms and finite effect inversion; and supplied a polynomial-size CLIQUE reduction whose guard, vertex, and edge weights force exactly an s-vertex lowest tied block. Exact scripts checked 210 graph/target instances through k=4, 1,536 weighted observation schedules, 120 one-missing sweeps, 145 inversion intervals, the 3/4-versus-1 constrained-support witness, and a case where equality faces raise 8/9 to 1. Current literature checks locate arbitrary-missing WMW tests and tie warnings but no supplied-design chamber optimizer or explicit-support hardness result. The cvcrand source confirms a generated support and a distinct residual-contrast test; only a new prespecified-endpoint rank option is claimed. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Machine-check the midrank subset-sum equality lemma and its lowest-tied-block consequence used by the CLIQUE converse. EARLY KILL TEST: Re-run internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/verify_exp_attrition_chamber_p1.py, requiring the equality-face result and every small CLIQUE equivalence; for any cvcrand adapter, enumerate sharp-null rejection mass and reject conditioning on survivors or the selected row. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The nearest result is Li, Sheng, and Yu's supremum Fisher p-value under attrition. Their extreme-completion simplification relies jointly on exchangeability and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention. The present kernel retains an arbitrary supplied rational assignment law and ordinary midranks, so the reference tail depends on the completed outcome weak order and equality faces can be optimal. Heng, Zhang, and Feng establish imputation-assisted randomization validity by re-imputing under reassignment and construct valid confidence regions, but their re-randomization law does not evaluate this supplied-support Wilcoxon-midrank completion envelope. The complete equality-inclusive chamber theorem, the \((2n+1)^k\) exact enumeration with a linear one-missing sweep, and the polynomial-bit \(\textsc{Clique}\) converse are therefore distinct field-level contributions. Zeng, Adams, and Bodenham already own arbitrary-missing Wilcoxon bounds and the warning that ties can decouple statistic and p-value extrema; the strict delta is the exact supplied-design tail optimizer and its computational frontier, not the general idea of worst-case rank testing.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 2 and 4, Theorem 1, Appendix A.3, and Discussion of arXiv:2507.00795v2.
seed_details.question: Can the worst-case Fisher upper tail under a supplied rational fixed-count design, treatment-indexed observation masks, and Wilcoxon midranks be represented exactly by all compatible complete weak orders, including equality faces?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The exchangeable rank law in Li, Sheng, and Yu no longer removes the completed outcomes from the reference distribution; the first replacement is a finite weak-order stratification on which every assignment-specific midrank sum is constant.
seed_details.destination_search: The supplied-design and weak-order pair was checked against Zeng, Adams, and Bodenham's Sections 3 and 5.2, Sills's tied-rank computation, Luo et al.'s arbitrary-mechanism Fisher theory, and current attrition-randomization manuscripts; no complete chamber optimizer was located.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee may call this immediate from Li, Sheng, and Yu because they already maximize Fisher p-values over missing completions.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their closed form uses exchangeable assignments and index tie-breaking; a supplied nonexchangeable law makes the entire tail depend on the completion, and midrank equality faces can strictly raise the optimum.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, distribution-free rank construction in Section 3, worst-case optimization in Section 4, and Discussion of arXiv:2507.00795v2.
seed_details.question: Is exact supplied-support optimization polynomial for every fixed number of missing outcomes but NP-complete when that number is part of the input?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The closed-form extremizer is replaced first by reversible insertion into ordered tie blocks, then by a bidirectional rational weighted-support reduction from \(\textsc{Clique}\).
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method pair was checked against Mehta, Patel, and Wei's design-specific exact recursions, Sills's coefficient extraction, and Karp's reduction framework; none classifies missing-completion optimization on an explicitly listed support.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may object that exponential enumeration already makes the problem computationally hard.
seed_details.rebuttal: Enumeration is not a lower bound; the explicit polynomial-bit \(\textsc{Clique}\) equivalence and membership certificate establish a genuine decision-complexity frontier.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 3--4, Proposition 1, Theorem 1, and Discussion of arXiv:2004.08472.
seed_details.question: Can the complete attrition-robust additive-effect confidence set be recovered by evaluating only observed treated--control residual crossings and their equality faces?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Luo et al.'s inversion treats one discrete p-value curve; here the first new step is to prove that the maximizing completion chamber can change only at an observed treated--control difference, while singleton breakpoint faces must be evaluated separately.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method pair was checked against Caughey et al.'s effect-increasing rank inversion, Li, Sheng, and Yu's attrition envelope, and Heng, Zhang, and Feng's re-imputation regions; none gives the weighted-support midrank breakpoint sweep.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say finite Fisher inversion is standard once pointwise p-values are available.
seed_details.rebuttal: The completion supremum changes its optimizer at residual crossings and equality faces can alter endpoint inclusion, so generic grid inversion or monotonicity does not recover the full confidence set.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, exact permutation comparison with midranks, examples on tied observations, and Conclusions in the published PLOS ONE article.
seed_details.question: Are lower-dimensional equality faces indispensable for exact worst-case tied-rank tails rather than removable by perturbation to strict orders?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step is to replace the usual generic-position perturbation by a direct block-midrank calculation, because a tie changes several assignment-specific sums simultaneously.
seed_details.destination_search: The equality-face question was checked against Zeng, Adams, and Bodenham's tie-dependent variance warning and Sills's fixed-sample tied null law; neither studies the supplied-design completion supremum.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may regard equality strata as measure-zero bookkeeping.
seed_details.rebuttal: The two-missing explicit instance has maximum \(1\) on an equality face but only \(8/9\) over every strict chamber, so deletion changes the exact answer.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, generating-polynomial construction for tied Wilcoxon laws, coefficient-extraction result, and concluding computational discussion of arXiv:2409.05741.
seed_details.question: Does one missing coordinate admit a linear sweep through observed tie blocks with constant-time rank updates per supported assignment?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Instead of recomputing a fixed tied distribution, maintain each row's treated-minus-realized doubled rank sum as the missing value crosses a block and update it by the block's treatment-column imbalance.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact tied-rank algorithms were searched for a moving missing coordinate and supplied assignment matrix; no linear face-inclusive sweep was located.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may call scanning \(2g+1\) positions obvious.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial part is the simultaneous exact update of all assignment-specific tail inequalities through equality half-steps, yielding \(O(n|\Omega|)\) rather than full reranking per face.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, constrained-space construction in Section 2, the \(\texttt{cptest}\) analysis in Section 3.4, and Summary of the R Journal article.
seed_details.question: Can a prospective Wilcoxon-midrank option reuse an ex ante saved constrained allocation space for exact attrition-robust cluster-endpoint inference without conditioning on survivors?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The residual-mean contrast is replaced by a prespecified scalar cluster endpoint, and each saved assignment must be evaluated with the completion envelope while the saved row probabilities remain unchanged.
seed_details.destination_search: The bridge was checked against Hennessy et al.'s ex ante conditional validity and Loh et al.'s warning against fixing the realized observed subset; no saved-support attrition-robust rank option was found.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may say this is merely a software wrapper around \(\texttt{cptest}\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The documented routine uses a different residual contrast and no missing-completion optimization; the claim is a new rank analysis on the unchanged prespecified support, not validity of the existing routine.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Sections 3--4 on polynomial coefficient extraction and computation, and Conclusion of arXiv:2409.05741.
seed_details.question: Can support-column symmetries quotient the weak-order tree without changing any assignment-specific treated-rank tail?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step groups missing units by identical columns in the explicit assignment matrix and selects a canonical nondecreasing block placement within each orbit.
seed_details.destination_search: Design-specific recursion and exact permutation computation were checked for orbit reductions driven by assignment columns; no completion-chamber quotient theorem was located.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may view identical-column pruning as elementary symmetry reduction.
seed_details.rebuttal: The rule is useful but not a standalone kernel; it is retained only as a certified optimization inside the complete chamber algorithm.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, computational-intractability discussion in Section 4, proof construction in Appendix A.3, and Discussion of arXiv:2507.00795v2.
seed_details.question: Is the explicit completion optimizer fixed-parameter tractable in \(k\), or is it \(\mathrm{W}[1]\)-hard under a support restriction that preserves the statistical interpretation?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The present \(\textsc{Clique}\) reduction has an \(n^{k}\)-scale chamber algorithm but does not yet give a parameter-preserving lower bound or an FPT dynamic program; the first step is to isolate support-column types and tie-block sufficient statistics.
seed_details.destination_search: Parameterized-complexity searches for Wilcoxon completion, missing-rank permutation tests, and explicit weighted randomization supports found no classification of this parameter.
seed_details.red_team: A referee may object that the question is detached from inference and may remain unresolved.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is retained explicitly as open content with a two-sided handle and is not used to support any theorem or complexity claim in the abstract.
